payload.setup: Crescent Energy agreed on 2026-10-08 to buy Devon Energy's Eagle Ford assets for about $4.2 billion in cash, and priced a $1 billion Class A share sale on 2026-10-09 at $12.50 a share. The stock closed at exactly $12.50 on 2026-10-15, so the market values the company at the price the new buyers paid, not above it.
payload.economic_basis: Crescent grows by buying oil and gas fields, and it pays with new debt and new shares. This deal adds about 90,000 net acres and a reported $140 million a year of cost savings, but the $1 billion share sale covers only part of the $4.2 billion cash price, so roughly $3.2 billion must come from debt, asset sales or both (my estimate from the reported figures). The common shareholder therefore owns a smaller part of a larger and more indebted company, and gains only if the added cash flow per share beats the added interest and the larger share count. The company has not disclosed the acquired production, reserves, purchase multiple, close date or pro forma debt, so that per-share test cannot be run yet. What is known is that the business already generates cash: the quarter ended 2026-06-30 showed about $944 million of operating cash flow and about $493 million of net income. Two things stay unknown and decide the call: how much debt the purchase adds, and how fast the bought wells decline.
evidence: Crescent agreed on 2026-10-08 to buy Devon Energy's Eagle Ford assets for about $4.2 billion in cash, covering about 90,000 net acres ([Benzinga, October 2026](https://www.benzinga.com/m/26/10/62241109/devon-energy-sell-its-eagle-ford-assets-crescent-energy-4-2b-cash)).

Crescent priced a $1 billion Class A offering at $12.50 for 80 million shares on 2026-10-09, and a KKR affiliate agreed to buy 40 million of them ([StockTitan 8-K summary](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CRGY/8-k-crescent-energy-company-reports-material-event-0a498471893d.html)).

The shares closed at $12.50 on 2026-10-15 after a 2.65% fall; the 1-month return was -11.38% and the 3-month return was +20.66%, and the quarter ended 2026-06-30 gave about $1.39 billion of revenue and $944 million of operating cash flow.

forecast.pricing_assessment: The shares sit at the $12.50 offer price, the level where the new buyers break even, so existing holders have no cushion. No measured consensus or valuation is available, so this call assumes the new supply outweighs any dealer support at $12.50.
assumptions: The banks that sold the shares do not hold the price at $12.50 for the whole week.
No new disclosure on funding or deal terms arrives inside the week.
Oil and gas prices stay near their recent levels.
forecast.opposing_case: A KKR affiliate bought 40 million of the 80 million new shares, so only half the new supply reaches the open market and that can steady the price. If buyers step in at the offer price, a short loses.

calls.hypothesis: The 80 million new shares are still being absorbed by the market, and sellers will hold the price at or below $12.50 through the week.
calls.invalidation: A close above $12.50 on rising volume, or news of a firm funding plan that lowers expected debt, would show the new supply is absorbed.
tail_risks: A jump in oil prices lifts all producers, including this one.
The company announces an asset sale that cuts expected debt.
A large investor buys stock in the open market.
evidence_limits: Whether the 80 million shares are new shares or stock sold by existing holders, because only new shares dilute.
The share count before and after the offering, to measure dilution per share.
The close date and funding plan for the $4.2 billion purchase.

forecast.pricing_assessment: At $12.50 the shares carry no credit for the reported $140 million of annual cost savings (my estimate of market treatment, not a measured expectation). With no disclosed purchase multiple or pro forma earnings, the evidence cannot size the downside.
assumptions: Most of the $4.2 billion comes from debt, not more equity or asset sales (estimate).
No pro forma cash flow per share figure appears during the month.
Oil and gas prices do not rise sharply.
forecast.opposing_case: The bought wells are mature Eagle Ford assets that produce steady cash, and the reported cost savings could make the deal add cash flow per share even after the extra interest. A strong third-quarter report and a clean funding plan could push the stock back above $12.50.

calls.hypothesis: The stock trades below $12.50 in one month because the extra debt and the larger share count reach the market before any proof of higher cash flow per share.
calls.invalidation: Disclosure that pro forma debt stays near current levels and that cash flow per share rises after the purchase would reverse this view.
tail_risks: A rise in oil or gas prices lifts cash flow and the share price.
The company sells non-core assets at good prices and cuts debt.
A large holder adds to its stake and absorbs the new supply.
evidence_limits: The acquired production, reserves and cash flow, to test the price paid per unit.
Pro forma debt and interest cost after the purchase.
How Crescent will fund the roughly $3.2 billion that the share sale does not cover (estimate).

forecast.pricing_assessment: The 3-month return of +20.66% shows the shares are still well above their mid-July level, so a further give-back has room. The short view rests on my estimate that interest and dilution cost more per share than the $140 million of savings, not on a measured valuation.
assumptions: The deal closes on schedule, and debt funds most of the price.
Oil and gas prices do not rise enough to lift cash flow per share above the added interest.
No large asset sale removes the new debt.
forecast.opposing_case: Eagle Ford assets bought at the low end of recent deal prices can add cash flow per share at once, and the stock rose 20.66% over three months, which shows buyers have accepted this buy-and-build model. If the first combined quarter shows higher cash flow per share, the short fails.

calls.hypothesis: By 2027-01-15 the shares trade below $12.50, because the market prices the higher debt and larger share count before it sees higher cash flow per share.
calls.invalidation: The first full quarter with the new assets showing higher cash flow per share and lower debt than before the deal would disprove this view.
tail_risks: A supply disruption lifts oil prices and the whole sector.
Crescent sells parts of the bought assets at a gain and cuts debt.
KKR or another large holder increases its stake and reduces the overhang.
evidence_limits: Third-quarter 2026 results, to compare operating cash flow with the prior quarter and separate one-off items.
Pro forma debt, interest cost and share count after the purchase and offering.
Whether the Eagle Ford assets carry hedges or firm transport duties that reduce their cash value.
